Below is a complete, practical architecture and repository plan for Samadhan Setu, designed for a two-person student team (fast to implement, easy to maintain, and extensible for AI capabilities).

High-level goals for the plan
- MVP in 4–8 weeks for a two-person team.
- Clear separation: frontend (React), backend (Node + TypeScript), DB (Postgres + pgvector), AI modules as service/adapters.
- CI, Docker, and simple infra choices so you can run locally and deploy easily.

Contents
1) Proposed repository folder structure  
2) Frontend architecture  
3) Backend architecture  
4) AI agent modules (design & responsibilities)  
5) Database schema (tables, key fields, indexes)  
6) Grievance taxonomy (categories, subcategories, severity)  
7) API endpoint design (paths, methods, major request/response shapes)  
8) First development milestone (tasks, timeline, owner split, acceptance criteria)  

1) Repository folder structure (single repo, backend + frontend)
- README.md
- .env.example
- docker-compose.yml
- /frontend
  - package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts
  - /public
  - /src
    - /assets
    - /components
    - /pages
    - /routes
    - /services (api client)
    - /state (React Query + Context)
    - /styles
    - /i18n
    - /utils
    - main.tsx, App.tsx
  - /tests (Jest/React Testing Library)
- /backend
  - package.json, tsconfig.json
  - /src
    - /config (env, constants)
    - /controllers (express routers)
    - /services (business logic)
    - /models (Prisma/TypeORM/Sequelize or types)
    - /repositories (DB access)
    - /ai (AI adapters / orchestrator)
    - /jobs (background jobs)
    - /middlewares (auth, validation, logging)
    - /utils
    - /workers
    - server.ts (app bootstrap)
  - /migrations (db migrations)
  - /tests (Jest)
- /infra
  - docker (Dockerfiles)
  - k8s manifests (optional)
  - /terraform (optional)
- /docs
  - api-spec.yaml (OpenAPI)
  - architecture.md
- .github (CI workflows)

Notes:
- Use a mono-repo with two subprojects to keep CI/commands simple.
- Keep AI logic isolated in /backend/src/ai so you can swap LLM providers without touching core logic.

2) Frontend architecture (practical, quick to implement)
Tech choices
- React + TypeScript + Vite (fast dev; easier learning curve than Next for two students)
- Styling: Tailwind CSS (fast) + small component lib (Headless UI / Radix UI)
- State: React Query (data fetching, cache, optimistic updates) + minimal Context for auth
- Router: React Router
- Forms: React Hook Form + Zod for validation
- File storage: uploads go to backend endpoint which stores to S3-compatible (MinIO in dev)
- i18n: react-i18next (multi-lingual)
- Testing: React Testing Library + Vitest or Jest

UI/Pages (MVP)
- Landing page / About
- Login / Register / Forgot password
- Dashboard (submit grievance, view statuses)
- Submit grievance wizard (choose category, describe, attach files, location metadata)
- Grievance detail (timeline, comments, attachments, status)
- Admin dashboard (list, filter, assign, comment, change status)
- Basic analytics/reporting (counts by category/status)

UX notes
- Keep forms short; use progressive disclosure (basic details first, optional details next).
- Show AI suggestions (category, summary) as non-blocking suggestions that user can accept/edit.

3) Backend architecture (scalable and pragmatic)
Tech choices
- Node.js + TypeScript
- Framework: Express (with TypeScript) or Fastify. Recommendation: Fastify for speed/async, but Express is fine for students. I'll recommend Express + TypeScript for simplicity.
- ORM: Prisma (excellent DX, type-safety, easy migrations). Postgres as primary DB + pgvector extension for embeddings.
- Auth: JWT (access + refresh) with role-based authorization (citizen, officer, admin). Passport.js optional but can roll simple middleware.
- File storage: S3-compatible (MinIO locally, AWS S3 for prod).
- Background jobs: BullMQ + Redis for email, heavy AI calls, async processing of attachments.
- Containerization: Docker + docker-compose for Postgres, Redis, MinIO.
- Monitoring: basic logging (pino/winston), error reporting (Sentry optional).
- API docs: OpenAPI (Swagger) auto-generated from routes or manual YAML in /docs.
- Tests: Jest for backend unit tests, supertest for integration.

Backend modules
- Auth module (login, register, refresh, roles)
- Users module (profiles, roles)
- Grievance module (create, update, status, comments, assignments)
- Search module (search & filter, full-text + vector search)
- AI module (classification, summarization, suggestions) — wrapper around LLM providers
- Attachments module (upload, presigned URLs)
- Notifications module (email/OTP/push)
- Admin module (reports, assignments, audit logs)

Security & Best Practices
- Validate and sanitize all inputs (Zod/Joi).
- Rate-limit public endpoints (e.g., create grievance).
- Store minimal PII; encrypt sensitive fields if needed.
- Signed pre-signed URLs for uploads; virus-scan attachments if possible.
- Role-based access checks on every protected endpoint.

4) AI agent modules (design & responsibilities)
High-level design: AI functionality is provided through a modular "AI service" layer with pluggable adapters for different providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, local model). Keep AI calls asynchronous via jobs when long-running, and synchronous only for quick tasks with rate limiting.

AI components (each as a separate module/service):
- Classifier
  - Goal: map free-text grievance -> category/subcategory + confidence score.
  - Implementation: initial rule-based + small fine-tuned classifier or prompt-based LLM call.
  - Output: category_id, subcategory_id, confidence.
- Summarizer
  - Goal: produce a short summary for display and for officer consumption.
  - Implementation: LLM summarization prompt; can run async.
- Entity Extractor / NER
  - Goal: extract names, locations, dates, IDs, organizations, phone numbers.
  - Implementation: LLM or spaCy/whitespace rules.
- Intent & Severity Detector
  - Goal: detect urgency (immediate harm vs routine), whether escalation needed.
- Responder / Resolution Recommender
  - Goal: suggest next steps (contact local office, accepted documents, forms).
  - Implementation: RAG (retrieval augmented generation) against knowledge base (policies, past resolved grievances).
- Embeddings & Search
  - Goal: embed grievances and knowledge articles into vector DB for similarity search.
  - Implementation: use embeddings API + store vectors in Postgres via pgvector (simple) or external vector DB as needed.
- Escalation engine
  - Rule-based + AI suggestions for escalation to higher authorities, with thresholds on response time and severity.
- QA & Moderation
  - Filter profanity, PII leakage, and misinformation; apply content flags.

AI architecture choices for students
- Use adapter pattern: backend/src/ai/adapter.ts with implementations for openai.ts, local.ts.
- For embeddings and vector search, start with pgvector (Postgres extension); it's easiest to run in docker-compose.
- Keep an "AI job" queue so heavy synchronous calls don't block HTTP requests.

Privacy & Safety
- Always show AI outputs as "suggestions" to humans.
- Store AI request/response for audit, with retention policy.
- Provide human-in-the-loop before automatic escalations.

5) Database schema (Postgres + pgvector outlines)
Note: Use Prisma or migration tool to define these. Below are core tables and primary fields.

Tables:
- users
  - id (uuid, PK)
  - email (unique)
  - password_hash
  - full_name
  - phone (nullable)
  - role (enum: citizen, officer, admin)
  - org_id (FK -> organizations)
  - locale
  - created_at, updated_at
- organizations
  - id, name, type (govt, ngo), parent_id
- departments
  - id, name, organization_id
- grievances
  - id (uuid PK)
  - external_ref (optional human-friendly ID)
  - user_id (FK -> users) — submitter
  - title
  - description (text)
  - category_id (FK)
  - subcategory_id (FK)
  - status (enum: submitted, triaged, in_progress, resolved, closed, escalated)
  - severity (enum: low, medium, high, critical)
  - assigned_to (FK -> users or NULL)
  - department_id (FK)
  - location (structured JSON: state,district,ward,lat,lng)
  - language
  - created_at, updated_at, resolved_at
- grievance_events (timeline entries)
  - id, grievance_id, actor_id, type (comment, status_change, assignment, escalation), content (text/json), created_at
- attachments
  - id, grievance_id, url, filename, content_type, size, uploaded_by, created_at
- comments
  - id, grievance_id, author_id, body, created_at, visibility (public/private)
- categories
  - id, name, parent_id (nullable), severity_default, description
- tags
  - id, name
- grievance_tags (many-to-many)
  - grievance_id, tag_id
- audit_logs
  - id, actor_id, action, meta(json), created_at
- embeddings
  - id (uuid)
  - source_type (grievance, kb_article)
  - source_id (uuid)
  - vector (pgvector)
  - created_at
- kb_articles (knowledge base)
  - id, title, body, tags, department_id, created_at
- assignments
  - id, grievance_id, assigned_to, assigned_by, created_at, status
- notifications
  - id, user_id, type, payload(json), sent_at, read_at
- rate_limits (optional)
  - ip/user, endpoint, window_ts, count

Indexes
- grievances: index(status), index(created_at), index(category_id), gin on text fields for full-text search
- embeddings: vector index (ivfflat) for efficient similarity search
- users.email unique

6) Grievance taxonomy (hierarchical, extensible)
Top-level categories and example subcategories. This should be configurable via admin.

1. Public Utilities
   - Water supply (no water, contaminated water)
   - Electricity (outage, meter malfunction, billing)
   - Sanitation (garbage not collected, blocked drains, sewage overflow)
2. Infrastructure & Roads
   - Road damage/potholes
   - Street lighting
   - Sidewalks/footpaths
3. Health & Medical
   - Hospital services (lack of staff, medicines)
   - Public health (immunization, outbreak)
   - Sanitation (vector control)
4. Education
   - School facilities
   - Teacher absenteeism
   - Admission problems
5. Social Welfare
   - Pension/benefits not received
   - Ration card issues, subsidy issues
6. Law & Order
   - Police response, crime reporting
   - Domestic violence (sensitive; route to special handling)
7. Environment
   - Illegal dumping
   - Pollution / factory emissions
8. Transport
   - Public transport availability
   - Traffic signals
9. Taxation & Revenue
   - Incorrect property tax billing
   - Stamp duty / property registration problems
10. Employment & Labor
    - Delay in payments, welfare scheme job issues
11. Land & Property
    - Encroachments, title disputes (high-sensitivity legal)
12. Digital Services & e-Governance
    - Portal not working, certificate issuance failures
13. Corruption & Grievance against officials
    - Bribery allegations (privacy + escalation)
14. Discrimination / Human Rights
    - Caste/Religion/Gender based discrimination

Additional metadata per grievance:
- Severity (low/medium/high/critical)
- Protected/Confidential flag (true/false)
- Sensitive category list (domestic violence, corruption, discrimination) — route to special handling/escalation

7) API endpoint design
Design principles:
- RESTful endpoints
- Standard JSON responses: { success: boolean, data: ..., error: {code, message} }
- Pagination: cursor or limit+offset (use cursor for scale but limit+offset ok for MVP)
- Versioning: /api/v1/...

Core endpoints (summary; you can expand with OpenAPI later)

Auth & Users
- POST /api/v1/auth/register
  - body: { email, password, full_name, phone, locale }
  - response: { user, tokens }
- POST /api/v1/auth/login
  - body: { email, password }
  - response: { user, tokens }
- POST /api/v1/auth/refresh
  - body: { refresh_token }
  - response: { access_token, refresh_token }
- GET /api/v1/users/me
  - headers: Authorization
  - response: user profile
- PUT /api/v1/users/me
  - update profile

Grievances
- POST /api/v1/grievances
  - create grievance
  - body: { title, description, category_id, subcategory_id (opt), location, attachments[], tags[], language }
  - response: created grievance
- GET /api/v1/grievances
  - list grievances (citizen sees own; admin sees filtered set)
  - query params: status, category_id, assigned_to, department, date_from, date_to, page, pageSize, search
  - response: { items: [...], meta: { total, page } }
- GET /api/v1/grievances/:id
  - detail including timeline, comments, attachments
- PUT /api/v1/grievances/:id
  - update (only allowed based on role and status)
- POST /api/v1/grievances/:id/comments
  - add comment (public/private)
- POST /api/v1/grievances/:id/assign
  - body: { assigned_to }
- POST /api/v1/grievances/:id/change-status
  - body: { status, note }
- GET /api/v1/grievances/:id/history
  - timeline

Attachments
- POST /api/v1/attachments/presign
  - body: { filename, contentType, size }
  - response: { upload_url, key } — backend validates and returns presigned URL to S3
- GET /api/v1/attachments/:id (returns metadata or presigned download URL)

Categories & Taxonomy
- GET /api/v1/categories
- POST /api/v1/categories (admin)
- PUT /api/v1/categories/:id

Search & AI
- GET /api/v1/search
  - q=..., filters...
  - supports full-text + vector-similarity flag
- POST /api/v1/ai/classify
  - body: { text }
  - response: { category_id, subcategory_id, confidence, candidates[] }
  - (For synchronous suggestions when user types)
- POST /api/v1/ai/summarize
  - body: { text, max_length }
  - response: { summary }
- POST /api/v1/ai/suggest-resolution
  - body: { grievance_id } or { text }
  - response: { suggestions: [ { action, rationale } ] }
- GET /api/v1/ai/embeddings/:source_id
  - for debugging

Admin & Reporting
- GET /api/v1/admin/metrics
  - response: counts by category/status, Avg resolution time, SLA violations
- POST /api/v1/admin/escalate
  - body: { grievance_id, target_role, reason }

Notifications
- GET /api/v1/notifications
- POST /api/v1/notifications/:id/read

Example: Create grievance request (abridged)
POST /api/v1/grievances
{
  "title": "No drinking water supply for 3 days",
  "description": "My area hasn't received water since 3 days — kids and elderly affected.",
  "category_id": "utilities.water",
  "location": { "state": "State", "district": "X", "ward": "12" },
  "attachments": ["key1", "key2"],
  "language": "hi"
}
Response:
{ "success": true, "data": { grievance object... } }

8) First development milestone (MVP) — practical split for two students
Objective: Deliver a functioning web app where citizens can register, submit a grievance (with attachments), view its status, and admins can view and update grievances. Minimal AI capability: a simple rule-based classifier that suggests a category (AI adapter stub that can be swapped later).

Duration: 4 weeks (intensive) or up to 6–8 weeks if working part-time.

Milestone deliverables (MVP)
- Basic infra & repo setup
  - Docker Compose bringing up: backend, frontend, Postgres, Redis, MinIO
  - Linting, Prettier, basic CI workflow (run tests)
- Authentication & Users
  - Register / Login / JWT token + refresh
  - User profile endpoint
- Grievance submission & display
  - Create grievance endpoint
  - Upload attachments via presigned URLs (MinIO)
  - Save grievance metadata in DB
  - Grievance listing for user (pagination, filters)
  - Grievance detail page with timeline & comments
- Admin interface (basic)
  - View list of grievances, filter by status/category
  - Assign grievance and update status
- AI: stub classification
  - When creating grievance, backend calls a stub classifier service that returns a category suggestion (rule-based or simple keyword map). Frontend shows suggestion and allows override.
- Search: basic text search (Postgres full-text)
- Tests: unit tests for core endpoints and UI smoke tests
- Documentation: README with local dev instructions and API spec for implemented endpoints

Suggested week-by-week split (4-week sprint)
- Week 0 (setup, day 1-2)
  - Create repo skeleton, Docker Compose, env files
  - Agree on tech choices, coding standards
- Week 1
  - Backend auth and user endpoints
  - Frontend auth flows and layout skeleton
- Week 2
  - Grievance creation backend + attachments presign + DB model
  - Frontend complaint form + uploads
- Week 3
  - Grievance list & detail pages
  - Admin list & basic assignment/action flow
  - Add comments and timeline
- Week 4
  - AI classification stub + show suggestions
  - Basic search
  - Tests, CI pipeline, README, deployment notes

Two-person task split (example)
- Developer A (frontend-focused)
  - UI layout, auth pages, grievance forms, dashboards, testing UI
  - Integrate React Query and API client
  - Accessibility & i18n basics
- Developer B (backend & infra)
  - API endpoints, DB models (Prisma), auth, presigned upload

Your proposed architecture is detailed, but I want to make some corrections before implementation.

1. TECH STACK
Use Python + FastAPI for the backend, React + TypeScript + Vite for the frontend, PostgreSQL for structured data and pgvector for vector retrieval.

Do not switch to Node.js or Express.

2. PRODUCT POSITIONING
Samadhan Setu is an AI-powered citizen grievance navigation and intelligence platform. It is NOT a government complaint management system.

We help citizens understand problems, identify responsible authorities, retrieve official procedures, prepare complaints and navigate existing grievance portals.

We do not independently assign complaints to government officers or claim to control government complaint statuses.

3. GRIEVANCE CATEGORIES

- Welfare and Government Schemes
- Public Sanitation and Waste Management
- Public Infrastructure
- Water and Electricity
- Public Healthcare Services
- Public Administration and Citizen Services

4. SIMPLIFY INFRASTRUCTURE
For the MVP, avoid Redis, BullMQ, MinIO, Kubernetes and unnecessary microservices.

5. CORE MVP WORKFLOW

- Describe a grievance.
- Receive AI-based classification.
- Provide location and relevant details.

1) Revised high-level architecture
- Single repository (monorepo) with frontend and backend folders.
- Backend: FastAPI app, modular code (api endpoints, agents/adapters for AI, services, models/ORM, database migrations). Use async FastAPI endpoints.
- AI: adapter pattern — a single ai/adapter interface with an OpenAI (or other LLM) adapter and a lightweight rule-based fallback. Use synchronous LLM calls for on-demand classification/generation — route heavy operations to FastAPI BackgroundTasks if needed (no Redis).
- Vector search: embeddings stored in Postgres using pgvector column. Retrieval is done with SQL using pgvector functions.
- File storage: local dev storage (uploads saved to /data/uploads), served via signed ephemeral URLs or proxied endpoints. For deployment, S3 can be swapped in later.
- Deployment: Docker Compose for local/dev with service containers: backend, frontend dev server (or built static serve), and postgres. Optionally a simple cloud deployment guide (Heroku/GCP Cloud Run/Azure Web Apps) for quick hackathon deployment.

Notes:
- Use SQLModel (from FastAPI author) or SQLAlchemy + Alembic. I recommend SQLModel for speed and FastAPI ergonomics, but SQLAlchemy+Alembic is fine if you prefer more control.
- Keep agents/ isolated so AI provider switching is painless.

3) Backend modules (detailed responsibilities)
- api.v1.grievances
  - create grievance (user description + optional attachments + location)
  - view grievance, update follow-up reference and manual status
- api.v1.ai
  - classify_text (returns category suggestion and confidence)
  - find_authority (returns likely authority + confidence + source references)
  - generate_complaint (structured complaint draft, editable)
- api.v1.attachments
  - upload endpoint(s) for local storage
- api.v1.analytics
  - anonymized dashboards (counts by category, volumes over time) with aggregation queries (no PII)
- agents.adapter
  - unified interface: classify(text), locate_authority(text, location), generate_complaint(structured_input), embed(text)
- services
  - GrievanceService: orchestrates db writes, AI calls and saves suggestions
  - AuthorityService: matches to authorities DB and produces source links
  - KBService: search knowledge_base + vector RAG lookup to return procedures

India has a large and fragmented public service delivery ecosystem.

4. Not knowing which documents or evidence are required.
